signal.title: Pretrained to Imagine, Fine-Tuned to Act: The Rise of World-Action Models
signal.summary: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。

editorial.intro: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。
editorial.why_it_matters: VLA 的记忆、推理和实时执行能力，直接决定具身智能能否从演示动作走向长时任务和真实部署。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对实验是否覆盖真实机器人、长时任务和跨场景泛化。

evidence.excerpt: Pretrained to Imagine, Fine-Tuned to Act: The Rise of World-Action Models | NVIDIA Technical Blog DEVELOPER Home Blog Forums Docs Downloads Training Join Technical Blog Subscribe Related Resources Robotics Pretrained to Imagine, Fine-Tuned to Act: The Rise of World-Action Models Jun 15, 2026 By Moritz Reuss Like Discuss (0) L T F R E AI-Generated Summary World-Action Models (WAMs) are emerging as a second major recipe for robot foundation models alongside VLM-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, using pretrained video backbones to predict future states and actions. Three core WAM formulations exist: inverse dynamics models that generate future video then infer actions, joint prediction models that emit video and actions together, and representation-only models that skip video generation at inference for faster execution. Action integration approaches include default action tokens, encoding actions as visual targets inside the video denoising interface, and compressing behavior into latent plans or actions learned from video.
